notes.decision: Translated 'host' provisionally. Lexeme is unattested in standard Coptic dictionaries; possibilities include (a) Greek χορός 'troop, choral host' (with unusual ⲍ for χ), (b) a Lyc. noun related to ⲥⲱⲣ 'spread, scatter' (cf. immediately following ⲉⲩⲥⲛⲣ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'spread out'), or (c) ϩⲱⲣ 'guardian.' Context ('the X of the archons being spread out, established among them, in upper/lower/outer/inner sides') requires a dispersive collective.
Read as Greek παράπτωμα + Coptic ⲗⲁⲩⲉ 'any' = 'any transgression,' with the construction ⲉⲙⲁⲍⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ + negative-particle 'holding back from any transgression.' Note Lyc. spelling ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲙⲡⲧⲟ for παραπτω-.

Translated 'the matter' provisionally. May be Lyc. ϩⲏⲡ 'hidden thing, secret' or ϩⲱⲡ 'judgment'; reduplicated ⲡⲡ unclear. The relative clause ⲉⲧⲁⲕ- 'which you (sg.)...' indicates an object the Living Spirit has done/uttered.

Translated 'they were gathered.' Verb unattested in standard Coptic; paired with ⲁⲩⲭⲉⲥⲧⲟⲩ ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'they were conveyed upward,' so a verb of gathering/binding/seizing fits. Possibly related to ⲕⲱⲙ̄ⲧ̄ 'gather' or a metathesis of ⲕⲙ̄ⲕⲙ̄ 'be silent.'

Translated 'furnace' on contextual grounds (paired with ⲣⲱⲭⲍ̄ 'burning' and ⲧⲥⲉⲧⲉ 'fire'). The lexeme is unattested; could possibly be a metallurgical implement or smelting vessel. Pictures the pre-cosmic refinement/binding of dark powers.
Read as ⲥⲁⲧⲉ 'shoot forth, sprout' with negative final clause: 'so that they might not put forth (shoots).' Fits agricultural register of bitter trees not putting forth bitter fruit (line 25).

Translated 'planted/plantings.' ⲧⲱⲟ̄ⲉ here = ⲧⲱϭⲉ 'plant, set in.' The verbal use 'they planted' and the cognate noun 'their plantings' both follow standard Manichaean agricultural-soteriological register (cf. ⲡⲱϩⲛ 'planting' in accumulated vocab).
Standard Lycopolitan abbreviation/contraction of ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ 'the Radiance' (accumulated vocab). Active verbal sense preserved.
